module.aws_eks_self_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.self_managed_ng: explicit depends_on of module.aws_eks_self_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_iam_role.self_managed_ng is redundant — already implied by attribute references

`null_resource.update_trust_policy` already references `aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution` in its local-exec command (`--role-name ${aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution.id}`), so this resource already depends on the role implicitly. The explicit `depends_on = [aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution]` is redundant.

`null_resource.update_trust_policy` already references `kubernetes_namespace.spark` in its local-exec command (`--namespace ${kubernetes_namespace.spark.id}`), so it already depends on the namespace implicitly. The explicit `depends_on = [kubernetes_namespace.spark]` is redundant.
`aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng` already depends on `aws_iam_role.managed_ng` through `node_role_arn = aws_iam_role.managed_ng[0].arn`, so listing it again in `depends_on` is redundant.

`aws_autoscaling_group.self_managed_ng` already depends on `aws_iam_instance_profile.self_managed_ng` transitively: it references `module.launch_template_self_managed_ng`, whose `launch_template_config` is built from `aws_iam_instance_profile.self_managed_ng[0].name`. The explicit `depends_on` on the instance profile is therefore redundant.

`aws_autoscaling_group.self_managed_ng` already depends on `aws_iam_role.self_managed_ng` transitively via `aws_iam_instance_profile.self_managed_ng` (which references the role) referenced through the launch-template module. The explicit `depends_on` on the role is redundant.

`module.aws_eks_teams` applies Kubernetes resources (namespaces, roles, role-bindings, service accounts, kubectl manifests) directly to the EKS API server. Unlike every other cluster-mutating module in this project (node groups, fargate, emr_on_eks, and the aws-auth config map), it only depends on `module.aws_eks` and does not gate on `data.http.eks_cluster_readiness`. Those Kubernetes apply operations can therefore race the not-yet-healthy API server right after cluster creation. The teams module should depend on `data.http.eks_cluster_readiness` (the same readiness gate used elsewhere).
